vendor_reported_contributing_factors: A latent lock-contention defect in the Microsoft 365 networking gateway had been present since a July 2026 change.
A Teams failover to the primary gateway changed traffic patterns and increased load on that gateway.
Nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity was unavailable due to an unrelated issue.
failure_chain: A latent software defect interacted with a changed traffic pattern and reduced capacity.
Gateway servers became unresponsive; reporting described more than 80 percent of the affected gateway fleet as unresponsive at the peak.
Traffic redistribution and restarting servers added load to the remaining capacity.
Backlogged traffic made recovery harder until the issue was identified and the gateway fix was deployed.

impact.customer_count_note: No verified normalized customer count is entered in this record.

security_assessment.status: Microsoft reported no evidence of malicious activity

lessons: Load tests must cover realistic traffic mixtures and the hardware SKU families that are actually deployed.
Failover can turn a local incident into a cascading failure if the receiving dependency has insufficient headroom.
Capacity health must include unavailable capacity, maintenance and degraded states.
Recovery requires queue drainage controls and should be load-tested separately from steady-state service.
